examples.text: Elle soupira en souriant, me jeta un regard de détresse qui signifiait : « Dieu ! que les hommes sont bêtes ! » […].

senses.note: En ce sens, il est ordinairement suivi de la préposition après

examples.text: Ils soupirent après 1919 et le wilsonnisme. Grand bien leur fasse. On sait ce que les couplets sur la dernière des guerres, le droit des nations à disposer d'elles-mêmes et ce messianisme humanitaire ont donné comme résultats.
Il y a longtemps qu’il soupirait après cette place, qu’il soupirait après cela.

glosses: Il s’emploie dans le même sens, avec la préposition « pour ».

examples.text: Il soupire pour cette femme.
J’ai longtemps soupiré pour vous.

glosses: Il est quelquefois transitif au figuré. (Il n’est d’usage ainsi qu’en poésie.)

examples.text: Soupirer ses peines.

glosses: A deep, prolonged audible inhale and exhale of breath; as when fatigued, frustrated, grieved, or relieved; the act of sighing.

examples.text: To Pollyanna the air was all the more stifling after that cool breath of the out of doors; but she did not complain. She only drew a long quivering sigh.

glosses: a manifestation of grief; a lament.

To inhale a larger quantity of air than usual, and immediately expel it; to make a deep single audible respiration, especially as the result or involuntary expression of fatigue, exhaustion, grief, sorrow, frustration, or the like.

examples.text: When she saw it wasn't damaged, she sighed with relief.
He sighed. It was going to be a long night.
He sighed over the lost opportunity.

A waiter brought his aperitif, which was a small scotch and soda, and as he sipped it gratefully he sighed.
 ‘Civilized,’ he said to Mr. Campion. ‘Humanizing.’ […] ‘Cigars and summer days and women in big hats with swansdown face-powder, that's what it reminds me of.’
He sighed deeply in his spirit.

glosses: To utter sighs over; to lament or mourn over.

examples.text: Ages to come, and men unborn, / Shall bless her name, and sigh her fate.

The lassie had grace given her to refuse, but with a woeful heart, and Heriotside rode off in black discontent, leaving poor Ailie to sigh her love. He came back the next day and the next, but aye he got the same answer.

glosses: To make a sound like sighing.

examples.text: And the coming wind did roar more loud, / And the sails did sigh like sedge.
The winter winds are wearily sighing.
She sighed a sigh that was nearly a groan.
sigh a note and sing a note
Never man sighed truer breath.

glosses: To express by sighs; to utter in or with sighs.

examples.text: "I guess I have no choice," she sighed.
She sighed her frustrations.
They […] sighed forth proverbs.
The gentle swain […] sighs back her grief.

glosses: An expression of fatigue, exhaustion, grief, sorrow, frustration, or the like, often used in casual written contexts.

examples.text: Sigh, I'm so bored at work today.

examples.text: I asked the doctor if I was long for this world

glosses: To have a desire for (a thing or an event).

examples.text: He was the object of my affection; I longed for him to notice me.
Oh how I long for this pandemic to end so we can go dancing again.
